 ATP Vienna – Flavio Cobolli withdraws in tears during match against Matteo Berrettini
 October 29, 2026 09:50 PM by Andrea Tebaldi Add as preferred source on Google SHARE © Instagram Flavio Cobolli / Fair Use The ATP 500 Vienna round-of-16 match between Flavio Cobolli and Matteo Berrettini ended in the worst possible way. Cobolli retired while trailing 5-2 in the first set, apparently because of a muscle injury.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 Cobolli was in tears after being forced to withdraw from the tournament. The extent of the injury will be assessed in the coming hours, with the Italian facing an intense period that includes tournaments in Paris, a possible bid to qualify for the ATP Finals in Turin and the Davis Cup Finals in Bologna.
 All of those events could now be at risk for the Rome-born player. Berrettini’s reaction, however, was widely praised. He immediately went over to comfort and embrace his friend and opponent, remaining with him until he left the court. It was the first official meeting between the two players and ended after just seven games, with Berrettini leading 5-2. 
 ATP Vienna: Berrettini advances after Cobolli retires
 The match had begun at a highly competitive pace, with several tightly contested games decided at deuce. The intensity was high, with five games played in the opening half-hour. Berrettini was the first to break serve, moving ahead 4-2 before extending his lead to 5-2. He consolidated the break in a game in which he fought back from 0-30.
 ADVERTISEMENT
 But when Cobolli was due to serve for the set, he was in tears and was forced to retire, apparently because of a muscle problem that raises serious questions about the remainder of his season.
 Berrettini will now face Alex de Minaur in the quarter-finals. The Vienna draw is already set for the last eight: Zverev will face Fery, Berrettini will play De Minaur, Mannarino will meet Medvedev and Paul will take on Carlos Alcaraz.
